newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Oil spill on frozen Siberian river said contained.
newsitem.headline: Oil spill on frozen Siberian river said contained.

text.p: A break in an oil pipeline has caused a 70-tonne oil spill in Surgut, a Western Siberian centre of Russian oil production, civil defence officials said on Sunday.

The oil spilled onto the frozen Chyornaya River on Friday but it has not mixed with the water because the river is frozen solid, an official at the local Civil Defence headquarters in Surgut said by telephone.
"There is no reason to be alarmed, it's a common technical breakdown and the consequences are being dealt with successfully," he said.
The oil from the pipeline, which is connected to about 250 oil wells, was contained as of Saturday night, he said.
The oil wells belonged to Surgutneftegaz, Russia's second largest crude oil producer.
Viktor Semyonov, a Surgutneftegaz official reached at civil defence headquarters, said: "Nothing extraordinary happened, it's an ordinary situation."
He declined to say if the accident had disrupted the company's oil output.
Local emergency ministry officials are investigating the reason for the spill, and company officials were working at the scene of the spill on Sunday.
